hints: Take natural logarithms of $3^y=4^{2-x}$ and use the power law.
Rearrange the result into the form $y=mx+c$.
Read the exact coefficient of $x$ as the gradient, leaving logarithms unevaluated.
walkthrough:
Take natural logarithms of both sides of the relation $3^y = 4^{2 - x}$:
$$\ln(3^y) = \ln(4^{2 - x})$$

Apply the power law of logarithms to bring the exponents down:
$$y\ln 3 = (2 - x)\ln 4$$

Divide both sides by $\ln 3$ to express $y$ in standard linear form $y = mx + c$:
$$y = \left(-\dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln 3}\right)x + \dfrac{2\ln 4}{\ln 3}$$
Since this equation is of the form $y = mx + c$ where $m = -\dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln 3}$ and $c = \dfrac{2\ln 4}{\ln 3}$ are constants, the graph of $y$ against $x$ is a straight line.

State the exact gradient of the line:
$$\text{Gradient} = -\dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln 3} \quad \left(\text{or } -\dfrac{2\ln 2}{\ln 3}\right)$$

hints: Use the straight-line relation $y\ln3=(2-x)\ln4$ from part (i).
Substitute $y=2x$ and collect all terms containing $x$.
Use $2\ln3+\ln4=\ln36=2\ln6$ to simplify the exact quotient.
walkthrough:
Substitute $y = 2x$ into the linear equation $y\ln 3 = (2 - x)\ln 4$:
$$(2x)\ln 3 = (2 - x)\ln 4$$

Expand the right-hand side and collect all terms involving $x$:
$$2x\ln 3 = 2\ln 4 - x\ln 4$$
$$2x\ln 3 + x\ln 4 = 2\ln 4$$
$$x(2\ln 3 + \ln 4) = 2\ln 4$$

Simplify the logarithmic coefficients using power and product laws:
$$2\ln 3 = \ln(3^2) = \ln 9$$
$$2\ln 3 + \ln 4 = \ln 9 + \ln 4 = \ln(9 \times 4) = \ln 36$$
$$2\ln 4 = \ln(4^2) = \ln 16$$

Express in terms of base logarithms using $\ln 36 = 2\ln 6$ and $\ln 16 = 2\ln 4$:
$$x(2\ln 6) = 2\ln 4 \implies x\ln 6 = \ln 4$$

Divide by $\ln 6$ to obtain the simplified exact $x$-coordinate:
$$x = \dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln 6} \quad \left(\text{or } \dfrac{2\ln 2}{\ln 6}\right)$$
